exposure: Causative bacterial pathogens (e.g., E. coli, Klebsiella spp., hemolytic streptococcus, CoNS, GBS)
Antimicrobial susceptibility patterns to various antibiotics (ciprofloxacin, vancomycin, meropenem, amikacin, Piperacillin-Tazobactam, ampicillin, cetofaxime)
outcome: Bacteriological profile of causative pathogens in EOS
Antibiotic susceptibility patterns of pathogens causing EOS
cohort: Neonates with proven positive blood cultures or cerebrospinal fluid admitted to eight neonatal intensive care units in the West Bank, Occupied Palestinian Territories, between January 2017 and December 2019.
finding: The study found an incidence rate of 3 per 1000 live births for culture-proven Early-Onset Sepsis, with E. coli and Klebsiella spp. being the most common gram-negative bacteria, and varying antimicrobial resistance patterns observed across pathogens.
cross-section timing: Data were retrieved retrospectively from January 2017 to December 2019.
